mishnah-berurah/1:א.en: (א) He is not permitted, etc. — there are many reasons among poskim: some wrote because of the mitzvah to recount the Exodus and Hashem's wonders even all night until sleep seizes him, as below — therefore he should not drink lest he become intoxicated and be nullified from this mitzvah; per this reasoning only wine or other intoxicating beverage; some wrote lest it appear he adds to the cups, as starting another meal — per this all strong wine from the country is forbidden even if not intoxicating; some wrote lest matzah taste be nullified from his mouth by drinking, as they forbade eating after the seder for this reason — per this any beverage even not strong wine from the country and not intoxicating is forbidden; from Mechaber and Rama it implies they hold to be strict for all these reasons; nevertheless Acharonim wrote ingber vasser and the like are permitted; some wrote even kreiznach is permitted as it does not nullify matzah taste and is like water [however for apple trank that crushes apples in the press and has strong taste, some forbid]. Even though l'chatchila it is proper to be strict on anything nullifying matzah taste, in great need one may rely on the first reason to permit other non-intoxicating beverages; and especially on the second night certainly one may be lenient on non-intoxicating beverages.
